assumptions: The record's annotations and Type-IIS sites follow one of the three published grammars.
limits: A part outside the three grammars is null, not a guess.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: The classification record itself: grammar, position, level and release enzyme, or null. The Parts Bin shows it as a row and the assembly's reading is on golden_gate_assemble.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which Golden Braid, MoClo or Yeast ToolKit grammar, position and level does this record represent?

description: Which Golden Braid / MoClo / Yeast ToolKit grammar, position and level the open plasmid represents (or null). Reads the record's own annotations, which is what lets an assembled transcription unit be recognised by its backbone half, and what lets a Level-0 module whose own backbone carries an extra site for the release enzyme be told from that backbone. Configured entry vectors are a Parts Bin concept and are NOT available here, so a TU sitting in a named acceptor is reported by its overhangs rather than by that acceptor's name.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

name: classify_grammar_part

classification.description: the full classification (null when no grammar matches)

grammar.description: grammar name, or empty when unclassified

isVector.description: true when a part at this position is also the acceptor backbone for its level (YTK Type 8, 8a, 678)

releaseCuts.description: how many times the release enzyme cut. 2 for a clean excise; 3 for a GoldenBraid Level-0 module, whose pUPD backbone carries its own site, so the backbone is released in two pieces and the insert is identified by carrying no backbone marker

spans.description: for a COMPOSITE position, the slots it occupies end to end (YTK Type 234 spans 2, 3 and 4); empty otherwise
